digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate and Gerrit DET backstop
propositions: Bug-fix plan reviews currently run only the light advisory tier (DET floor + necessity probe) with all findings downgraded to advisory, allowing complex fixes with substantive design changes to land without full rubric review.

Explicit review-plan on a bug with persisted non-test file_impact must escalate to the full blocking rubric, covering both the precheck and route_criteria seams plus the batch-runner fan-in, while test-only and empty file_impact remain at light tier.

Gerrit DET criterion must block oversized bug fixes (>150 non-test lines, excluding tests/** and conftest.py) lacking a current or code-drifted attestation, reading attestations cross-host via opcert verification with the trusted-environment machinery.

Attestation verdict predicate accepts certified/stale-code/stale-head, flags remaining plan-review compute_validity literals and op-cert verification failures, and fails open (advisory only) on infrastructure errors or unknown verdicts.
Backtest over 113 historical bug-fix commits confirms that the 150-line threshold with non-test classification flags exactly the 13 hand-adjudicated substantive commits with zero false positives.
Claim-time bug exemption and light advisory tier for small/test-only fixes remain unchanged; no CLI --size-lines flag or step-input schema changes required.
